mcq.q: What is the solid waste passed out through the anus called?
mcq.explanation: Faeces are the solid waste of the body.

mcq.q: What does the rectum do?
options: Stores faeces for a short time
mcq.explanation: The rectum stores faeces before they pass out.

mcq.q: Which part of the digestive system is the widest tube near the end?
mcq.explanation: The large intestine is wider than the small intestine.

mcq.q: Which part of the digestive system is long and coiled?
mcq.explanation: The small intestine is a very long coiled tube.

mcq.q: Why should you chew your food well?
options: It makes food smaller for easier digestion
mcq.explanation: Chewing breaks food into small pieces.

mcq.q: Which of these helps to keep teeth healthy?
mcq.explanation: Brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

mcq.q: Why should you limit sweets and sugary drinks?
mcq.explanation: Sugar feeds germs that damage teeth.

mcq.q: What does deworming do?
mcq.explanation: Deworming tablets kill worms living in the intestines.

mcq.q: Why should you wear shoes and wash hands to prevent worms?
options: Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
mcq.explanation: Worm eggs can enter the body through dirt.

mcq.q: Which food group helps to prevent constipation?
mcq.explanation: Fibre helps food move through the intestines.

mcq.q: Which of these is a symptom of an unhealthy digestive system?
mcq.explanation: Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation are digestive symptoms.

mcq.q: What is diarrhoea?
options: Passing loose watery faeces many times
Food coming out of the mouth
mcq.explanation: Diarrhoea means loose watery faeces.

mcq.q: What is constipation?
options: Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
mcq.explanation: Constipation means hard faeces that are difficult to pass.

mcq.q: What is vomiting?
options: Food coming out through the mouth
mcq.explanation: Vomiting is throwing up food through the mouth.

mcq.q: What is bloating?
options: A full, swollen tummy often with gas
mcq.explanation: Bloating means the tummy feels full and swollen.

mcq.q: Why is diarrhoea dangerous for young children?
mcq.explanation: The body loses a lot of water and can become weak.

mcq.q: What can help a child with diarrhoea while waiting to see a health worker?
options: Drinking clean water and ORS as advised
mcq.explanation: Water and ORS replace what the body loses.

mcq.q: Which of these is a healthy habit for digestion?
options: Eating food that fell in dirt
Drinking water from a dirty pond
mcq.explanation: Clean hands prevent germs from entering the mouth.

mcq.q: Why should fruits and vegetables be washed before eating?
mcq.explanation: Washing removes dirt, germs and worm eggs.

mcq.q: Which of these is a balanced meal?
mcq.explanation: A balanced meal has energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.

mcq.q: What should you do when you have a persistent stomach ache?
options: Tell an adult and see a health worker
mcq.explanation: Adults and health workers can help find the cause.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a part of the digestive system?
mcq.explanation: Lungs are for breathing.

mcq.q: What is the job of the anus?
options: To let faeces leave the body
mcq.explanation: The anus is the opening at the end of the digestive tube.

mcq.q: Which of these is true about the small intestine?
options: Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
mcq.explanation: Absorption takes place there.

mcq.q: Which of these do we drink to keep digestion healthy?
mcq.explanation: Clean safe water helps digestion and prevents disease.

mcq.q: In the mouth, which part helps to move food around and swallow?
mcq.explanation: The tongue moves food and helps swallowing.

mcq.q: Which of these parts is found before the stomach?
mcq.explanation: Food passes through the gullet before it reaches the stomach.

mcq.q: Which of these parts is found after the stomach?
mcq.explanation: Food moves from the stomach to the small intestine.

mcq.q: A pupil has hard dry faeces. Which is the best advice?
options: Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water
mcq.explanation: Fibre and water help soften faeces.

mcq.q: Which of these can cause stomach ache?
options: Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
mcq.explanation: Fast eating and dirty food can cause stomach pain.

mcq.q: How often should teeth be brushed?
mcq.explanation: Brushing morning and night keeps teeth healthy.

mcq.q: Which of these helps prevent germs entering the food?
mcq.explanation: Covering food keeps out flies and dirt.

mcq.q: The stomach is described in the lesson as being like
mcq.explanation: The stomach is a stretchy bag that churns food.

mcq.q: Why is it important to eat slowly?
options: It lets you chew well and helps digestion
It makes food taste of salt
mcq.explanation: Chewing well breaks food down before swallowing.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way of storing leftover food safely?
options: Leaving it uncovered in the sun
Covering it and keeping it clean
mcq.explanation: Covered food is safer from germs.

mcq.q: Which of these describes healthy eating?
options: Eating fruits, vegetables and whole grains
mcq.explanation: Healthy eating includes fibre and a variety of foods.

mcq.q: Why is a plan for a healthy digestive system useful?
options: It cures all diseases at once
It reminds us to do the right things every day
mcq.explanation: A plan helps us follow healthy habits.

mcq.q: What does the large intestine do with the leftovers?
options: Takes back water and forms faeces
mcq.explanation: Water is absorbed and the rest becomes solid waste.

mcq.q: Which of these leaves the body through the anus?
mcq.explanation: Faeces leave the body through the anus.

mcq.q: What does the small intestine mainly absorb?
mcq.explanation: Digested food passes through its wall into blood.

mcq.q: Which of these is a good use of a school deworming day?
options: Take the tablets when given by the health worker
mcq.explanation: Follow the health worker's advice.

mcq.q: What are the symptoms of worms mentioned in the lesson?
options: Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
mcq.explanation: These are signs that worms may be present.

mcq.q: What is matter?
options: Anything that has mass and takes up space
mcq.explanation: Matter has mass and occupies space.

mcq.q: Which of these is matter?
mcq.explanation: Water has mass and takes up space. Light, sound and heat are not matter.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT matter?
mcq.explanation: Light has no mass and takes up no space.

mcq.q: What does mass mean?
options: The space an object takes up
The amount of matter in an object
mcq.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in something.

mcq.q: What does volume mean?
options: The amount of matter in an object
The amount of space an object takes up
mcq.explanation: Volume is the space a substance takes up.

mcq.q: Which are the three states of matter?
mcq.explanation: Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.

mcq.q: Which state of matter has its own shape and fixed volume?
mcq.explanation: Solids keep their shape and volume.

mcq.q: Which of these is a solid?
mcq.explanation: A stone keeps its shape.

mcq.q: Which of these is a liquid?
mcq.explanation: Cooking oil flows and takes the shape of its container.

mcq.q: Which of these is a gas?
mcq.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases.

mcq.q: What happens to a liquid when you pour it into a different container?
options: It takes the shape of the new container
mcq.explanation: A liquid has no shape of its own.

mcq.q: What happens to a gas that is put in a closed jar?
options: It spreads to fill the whole jar
It sits at the top only
mcq.explanation: A gas fills any container it is in.

mcq.q: Which of these is true of a liquid?
options: It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume
mcq.explanation: A liquid has a fixed volume and takes the container's shape.

mcq.q: Which of these is true of a gas?
options: It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
mcq.explanation: A gas spreads to fill the space.

mcq.q: Which of these is true of a solid?
options: It takes the shape of any container
It keeps its shape wherever it is put
mcq.explanation: A solid has a definite shape.

mcq.q: What instrument measures the mass of an object?
mcq.explanation: A balance is used to measure mass.

mcq.q: What instrument measures the volume of a liquid?
mcq.explanation: A measuring jug or cylinder shows volume.

mcq.q: Which unit is used for the mass of a sack of maize?
mcq.explanation: Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

mcq.q: Which unit is used for the volume of milk?
mcq.explanation: Liquid volume is measured in millilitres and litres.

mcq.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
mcq.explanation: 1 litre is 1000 ml.

mcq.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
mcq.explanation: 1 kg is 1000 g.

mcq.q: How many millilitres are in 2 litres?
How many grams are in 5 kg?
A jug has 400 ml of water. Fatuma adds 250 ml. How much water is in the jug?
A bag has 1 kg of rice and 250 g of beans. What is the total mass?
There are 750 ml of milk in a jug. 300 ml is poured out. How much is left?
Why is air matter?
options: It has mass and takes up space
mcq.explanation: Air fills balloons and pushes against things, so it takes up space.

mcq.q: Which activity shows that air takes up space?
mcq.explanation: The balloon swells because air takes up space inside.

mcq.q: In the dry tissue experiment, why does the tissue stay dry?
options: Air in the cup keeps the water out
The cup is made of plastic
mcq.explanation: Air takes up the space inside the cup.

mcq.q: Sand pours like a liquid. What state is each grain?
mcq.explanation: Each grain is a small solid.

mcq.q: Which of these can be poured and takes the shape of its container?
mcq.explanation: Water is a liquid.

mcq.q: A kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same
mcq.explanation: Both are 1 kg. The feathers take up much more space.

mcq.q: Steam from a boiling pot is really
mcq.explanation: Steam is water as a gas and is invisible. The cloud we see is tiny water drops.

mcq.q: Which of these gases do we breathe in to stay alive?
mcq.explanation: Oxygen in the air is needed for life.

mcq.q: Which state of matter is used in a cooking gas cylinder?
mcq.explanation: Cooking gas is a gas that burns to give heat.

mcq.q: Why are solids like bricks and stones used to build houses?
options: They keep their shape and can support weight
mcq.explanation: Solids keep their shape.

mcq.q: Why are liquids useful for drinking?
options: They can be poured and swallowed
mcq.explanation: Liquids pour easily.

mcq.q: What does a football need to keep its shape?
mcq.explanation: The air inside fills the football.

mcq.q: Which of these can be a solid, liquid or gas depending on conditions?
mcq.explanation: Water can be ice, liquid water or steam.

mcq.q: Why should each child use their own balloon for the balloon activity?
mcq.explanation: Sharing a balloon that has been in someone's mouth can spread germs.

mcq.q: Which of these is a liquid used as fuel?
mcq.explanation: Paraffin and petrol are liquid fuels.

mcq.q: Which of these solids can be poured?
mcq.explanation: Flour is made of tiny solid grains that can pour.

mcq.q: Which of these is heavier: 3 kg of sugar or 3000 g of sugar?
mcq.explanation: 3 kg equals 3000 g.

mcq.q: A cup can hold about
mcq.explanation: A cup holds about 250 ml.

mcq.q: When reading a measuring jug, where should your eye be?
options: At the same level as the water surface
mcq.explanation: This gives an accurate reading.

mcq.q: Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume?
mcq.explanation: Gases spread out to fill all the space.

mcq.q: An empty bottle is full of
mcq.explanation: An empty bottle contains air.

mcq.q: Which of these is a correct grouping?
options: Air, stone and salt are gases
Chalk, water and steam are solids
Milk, water and juice are liquids
Steam, oil and rice are gases
mcq.explanation: Milk, water and juice are all liquids.

mcq.q: Which grouping of gases is correct?
options: Sugar, oil and air are solids
Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
Stone, water and wood are liquids
Milk, chalk and steam are solids
mcq.explanation: Air, steam and cooking gas are gases.

mcq.q: A heavy sack of maize has more mass than a small packet of salt. This means the sack has more
mcq.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter.

mcq.q: Which of these do we measure using litres?
mcq.explanation: Litres measure volume.

mcq.q: Which of these is a reason we need gases?
options: We can build houses with them
mcq.explanation: Air gives us oxygen for breathing.

mcq.q: Which of these statements about matter is correct?
options: Solids, liquids and gases all have mass
mcq.explanation: All matter has mass, whatever its state.

mcq.q: What is solid waste?
options: Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
mcq.explanation: Solid waste is unwanted solid material.

mcq.q: Which of these is solid waste?
mcq.explanation: A banana peel is a solid thrown away.

mcq.q: What is decomposable waste?
options: Waste that rots and breaks down
mcq.explanation: Decomposable waste is broken down by decomposers.

mcq.q: Which of these breaks down and rots easily?
mcq.explanation: Vegetable peelings are decomposable.

mcq.q: Which of these is non-decomposable?
mcq.explanation: Plastic does not rot easily.

short.q: What is meant by water conservation?
short.answer: Using water carefully and protecting water sources so that there is enough for everyone.
short.working: 1 mark for careful use and 1 mark for protecting or enough for everyone.

short.q: Give two ways in which water is wasted at school.
short.answer: Leaving taps running, leaking taps or pipes, using too much water for washing.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: State two reasons for conserving water.
short.answer: To have enough water for all, to save money, for crops and animals, to protect sources.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: A tap leaks 4 litres every hour. How much water is lost in 6 hours?
short.answer: 24 litres.
short.working: 1 mark for 4 x 6 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

short.q: Name two things a farmer can do to save water.
short.answer: Use drip irrigation, use mulch, water at cooler times, harvest rainwater.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain the difference between reducing and reusing water. Give one example of each.
short.answer: Reducing means using less water, for example closing the tap. Reusing means using the same water again, for example using washing water for the garden.
short.working: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for examples.

short.q: Describe how rainwater can be harvested from a school roof.
short.answer: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter. The gutter leads to a pipe which fills a covered tank.
short.working: 1 mark for roof and gutter, 1 mark for pipe, 1 mark for tank.

short.q: Give three ways of saving water at home.
short.answer: Close taps, use a cup or basin, fix leaks, use a bucket instead of a hose, reuse washing water.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Why is used washing water not safe for drinking? Give one good way to use it.
short.answer: It has dirt and germs. It can be used to water plants or mop floors.
short.working: 1 mark for dirty water, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for a safe use.

short.q: A school tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much water is lost in a school day of 8 hours and in 5 school days?
short.answer: 16 litres in one day and 80 litres in five days.
short.working: 1 mark for 2 x 8, 1 mark for 16, 1 mark for 16 x 5 = 80.

short.q: Give three ways of protecting water sources.
short.answer: Plant trees near rivers, do not throw waste in water, do not wash in springs, keep animals away from drinking sources.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why a rainwater tank should have a lid.
short.answer: It keeps out dirt and leaves and stops mosquitoes from breeding in it.
short.working: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for mosquitoes, 1 mark for making water safer.

short.q: Describe how a poster can teach the community about water conservation. Give four features.
short.answer: A clear message, big pictures, short slogan, bright colours, ideas for saving water, placed where many people see it.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four features.

short.q: Explain how wasting water can affect other people and the family.
short.answer: Less water is left for others, especially in dry areas. The family pays more for water and may have to fetch more.
short.working: 2 marks for others and 2 marks for family.

short.q: Explain how drip irrigation and mulching save water.
short.answer: Drip irrigation sends water drop by drop to the roots so little is lost. Mulch covers soil so less water evaporates.
short.working: 2 marks for each method.

short.q: List four water-saving habits that pupils can practise at school.
short.answer: Close taps, report leaks, use a bucket for watering the garden, water plants in the morning or evening, use a cup to drink.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Describe three examples each of reducing and reusing water.
short.answer: Reduce: close taps, fix leaks, use a cup. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants, laundry water for mopping, rainwater for the garden.
short.working: Award marks for correct examples up to a total of 4.

short.q: Explain the importance of conserving water at home and school.
short.answer: There is enough water for all, we save money, animals and crops get water, it reduces work of fetching water and protects sources.
short.working: 1 mark for each reason up to 5.

short.q: Describe the methods of conserving water. Include reducing, reusing and recycling with examples.
short.answer: Reduce wastage: close taps. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants. Recycle: cleaning used water at a treatment plant or filtering. Include rainwater harvesting.
short.working: 1 mark for each of three methods, 1 mark for correct examples and 1 mark for harvesting.

short.q: Plan a project to sensitise your community about the importance of water conservation. State the steps.
short.answer: Choose a message, make posters, put them near taps and gates, speak at assembly, do a demonstration of saving water and check results.
short.working: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

short.q: A family of five uses a tap that drips 1 litre every hour. Calculate how much water is wasted in one week and suggest what they should do.
short.answer: 24 x 7 = 168 litres. They should repair the tap or ask an adult or plumber to fix it.
short.working: 1 mark for 24 hours, 1 mark for 24 x 7, 1 mark for 168, 1 mark for fixing the tap, 1 mark for units.

short.q: What is a force? Give one example of a push and one example of a pull.
short.answer: A force is a push or a pull. A push: kicking a ball. A pull: opening a drawer.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the two examples.

short.q: Name the two forces studied in this topic.
short.answer: Gravity and friction.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: State two ways of reducing friction.
short.answer: Smoothen surfaces, use oil or grease, use rollers, use ball bearings.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Give two effects of force on objects.
short.answer: Change shape, start motion, stop motion, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction, hold things together.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain why rubbing your hands makes them warm.
short.answer: Rubbing causes friction and friction produces heat.
short.working: 1 mark for friction and 1 mark for heat.

short.q: Explain what gravity is and give two examples of its effects.
short.answer: Gravity is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth. It makes rain fall and makes a thrown ball come down.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each example.

short.q: Describe how you can show that rough surfaces give more friction than smooth ones.
short.answer: Slide the same block down a ramp covered with different surfaces. It travels a shorter distance on rough surfaces than on smooth ones.
short.working: 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Give three uses of friction in daily life.
short.answer: Brakes, shoes gripping the ground, lighting matches, rough tyres, sharpening tools.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Give three problems caused by friction.
short.answer: It wears away shoes and tyres, wastes energy, makes machines hot and slows moving parts.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: A ball is at rest. Kelvin kicks it, then Mercy stops it with her foot, then she kicks it to the right. Name the effect of the force in each case.
short.answer: Kelvin starts motion, Mercy stops motion, Mercy's second kick changes direction.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct effect.

short.q: Explain why the flat paper and stone dropped together do not land at the same time.
short.answer: Gravity pulls both down but air pushes up on the flat paper more, so it falls slowly. The stone is little affected by the air.
short.working: 1 mark for gravity on both, 1 mark for air pushing paper, 1 mark for stone landing first.

short.q: Give three examples where a force holds objects together.
short.answer: Glue holding paper, nails holding wood, rope tying things, stitches holding cloth, screws.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Describe how a wheelbarrow makes work easier and how it is looked after.
short.answer: The wheel rolls so friction with the ground is small. It is easier to push than drag a load. Oil the joints and wheel axle to reduce friction.
short.working: 1 mark for wheel, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for oil, 1 mark for care.

short.q: Explain how ball bearings help a bicycle move.
short.answer: They are small steel balls in the wheel. They roll between moving parts, so there is less friction and the wheels turn easily.
short.working: 1 mark for what they are, 1 mark for rolling, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for wheels turning easily.

short.q: Describe four effects of forces using examples from daily life.
short.answer: A force changes the shape of dough, starts a ball moving, stops a bicycle with brakes and changes the direction of a ball when hit with a stick.
short.working: 1 mark for each effect with an example.

short.q: Describe how you would do an activity to show gravity.
short.answer: Drop a stone and a ball from the same height. Observe that they fall down to the ground. Gravity pulls them down.
short.working: 1 mark for items, 1 mark for dropping, 1 mark for observing downward fall, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Explain why friction can be both useful and a problem. Give two examples of each.
short.answer: Useful: brakes stop bicycles and shoes grip the ground. A problem: it wears out tyres and makes machines hot.
short.working: 1 mark for saying it helps in some cases and harms in others, and 1 mark for each correct example up to 3.

short.q: A block is pulled along a rough floor and along a smooth floor with the same force. Describe and explain what you would see.
short.answer: The block moves slower or a shorter distance on the rough floor. Rough floors give more friction.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four points.

short.q: Describe how to investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction using a ramp and a block. Include what you keep the same.
short.answer: Make a ramp. Slide a block down it covered with cloth, paper, cardboard and bare board. Measure how far it slides each time. Keep the same block, same ramp height and same push. Record in a table. The shortest distance shows the most friction.
short.working: 1 mark for ramp, 1 mark for surfaces, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for fair test, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Explain how gravity helps and how it can cause problems in daily life.
short.answer: It keeps us on the ground, makes rain fall and water flow downhill. It can make objects fall and cause injuries and break things.
short.working: 2 marks for help and 2 marks for problems and 1 mark for a clear explanation.

short.q: Describe five ways in which forces are used at home and on the farm.
short.answer: Pushing a wheelbarrow, pulling a plough, lifting water from a well with a rope, hammering a nail, kicking a ball, stitching clothes.
short.working: 1 mark for each use.

short.q: Explain why we should reduce friction in machines and how it can be done.
short.answer: Friction wears out parts, wastes energy and makes machines hot. It is reduced by oiling, smoothing, using rollers or ball bearings.
short.working: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for methods.

short.q: Give two natural and two artificial sources of light.
short.answer: Natural: sun, stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: bulb, torch, candle, lantern, solar lamp.
short.working: 1 mark for two correct natural and 1 mark for two correct artificial.

short.q: Why is the moon not a source of light?
short.answer: It does not make its own light. It reflects light from the sun.
short.working: 1 mark for no light of its own and 1 mark for reflecting sunlight.

short.q: State two uses of light.
short.answer: To see, for safety, to discourage pests, for plants to make food, to dry clothes.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Name two ways of lighting a house during the day.
short.answer: Windows and translucent roof sheets (skylights).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Give two examples each of transparent and opaque materials.
short.answer: Transparent: clear glass, clear plastic, clean water. Opaque: wood, metal, stone.
short.working: 1 mark for each pair.

short.q: Describe how you would show that light travels in a straight line.
short.answer: Use three cards with holes in the middle and line them up in a row. Shine a torch through the holes. Light passes. Move the middle card and the light is blocked.
short.working: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials.
short.answer: Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials do not let light through.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Give three ways of lighting a house at night.
short.answer: Electric bulbs, solar lamps, paraffin lamps, candles.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain how light helps in security and safety. Give three examples.
short.answer: Street lights help people see, security lights keep thieves away, traffic lights direct drivers, torches show dangers, reflectors.
short.working: 1 mark for each example.

short.q: Explain why a translucent roof sheet is useful in a classroom during the day.
short.answer: It lets daylight in, so lamps are not needed, saving electricity and money.
short.working: 1 mark for daylight, 1 mark for no lamps, 1 mark for saving.

short.q: Give three safety rules when using sources of light.
short.answer: Never look directly at the sun, do not shine torches in eyes, keep candles and lamps away from curtains and paper, do not touch hot bulbs.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain why a mirror or a shiny cup is not a source of light.
short.answer: It does not make its own light. It only reflects light that falls on it.
short.working: 1 mark for not making light, 1 mark for reflecting, 1 mark for explanation.

short.q: Classify these as natural or artificial: candle, stars, torch, lightning, firefly, solar lamp.
short.answer: Natural: stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: candle, torch, solar lamp.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair, plus 1 mark for correct table.

short.q: Describe how windows, roofs and walls can be used to make a house brighter by day.
short.answer: Large windows let in light, translucent roof sheets let in light, light-coloured walls reflect light, open curtains.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four points.

short.q: A pupil wants to find out which material is transparent, translucent or opaque. Describe a test.
short.answer: Use a torch in a dark room. Put tissue paper, clear plastic and a book one at a time between the torch and a wall. Record whether all, some or no light passes.
short.working: 1 mark for equipment, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for classification.

short.q: Explain how farmers use light to discourage pests and animals.
short.answer: They use bright or flashing lights at night near fields or animal pens to scare wild animals away. Lamps near sheds help to see thieves or pests.
short.working: 1 mark for bright lights, 1 mark for scaring away animals and 2 marks for examples.

short.q: Why should we use LED and solar lamps instead of paraffin lamps? Give two reasons.
short.answer: They are safer with less fire risk and less smoke. Solar lamps use free energy and are cheaper to use.
short.working: 2 marks for each reason.

short.q: Explain why light is important in our daily lives.
short.answer: It lets us see, keeps us safe, helps plants to make food, dries clothes, gives solar power and discourages pests.
short.working: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

short.q: Describe the natural and artificial sources of light and explain the difference.
short.answer: Natural sources are found in nature such as the sun, stars, lightning and fireflies. Artificial sources are made by people such as bulbs, torches and candles.
short.working: 1 mark each for natural and artificial, 1 mark for examples of each and 1 mark for the difference.

short.q: Discuss how a family can light their home cheaply and safely.
short.answer: Use windows and translucent sheets by day, solar lamps and LED bulbs at night, keep candles and paraffin away from cloth, turn off lights when not needed.
short.working: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

short.q: Name the three main sources of heat.
short.answer: The sun, fire and electricity.
short.working: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

short.q: State two uses of heat at home.
short.answer: Cooking, warming, ironing, drying clothes.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Why do we use kitchen gloves when holding hot pots?
short.answer: Gloves are poor passers of heat so they protect hands from burns.
short.working: 1 mark for poor at passing heat and 1 mark for protection from burns.

short.q: Give two safety rules when using an electric iron.
short.answer: Do not touch it while hot, switch off after use, keep it away from children, do not touch with wet hands.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: What is evaporation? Give one example.
short.answer: Liquid water turning into water vapour, for example wet clothes drying.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for an example.

short.q: Describe how to show that metal passes heat more easily than wood.
short.answer: Put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon into a cup of warm water. After two minutes touch the top of each. The metal feels warmer so metal passes heat easily.
short.working: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Give three safety measures to observe when cooking.
short.answer: Use gloves, turn handles inwards, keep children away, do not play with matches, keep paraffin away from fire.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain how wet clothes dry in the sun.
short.answer: Heat from the sun makes the water evaporate. It changes to vapour and goes into the air so the clothes become dry.
short.working: 1 mark for sun heat, 1 mark for evaporation, 1 mark for the result.

short.q: What should you do for a small burn? State three actions.
short.answer: Put it under cool running water, cover with a clean cloth, tell an adult and do not put butter or oil.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Give three examples of things that use electricity to make heat.
short.answer: Electric kettle, iron, cooker, heater, hair dryer, toaster.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why heat from the sun is important to the Earth.
short.answer: It warms the Earth so plants and animals can live, it dries things, and helps the water cycle.
short.working: 1 mark for each of three points.

short.q: Why should you not touch a hot object to find out how hot it is? What should you use?
short.answer: It can burn your skin. Use a thermometer.
short.working: 1 mark for burns, 1 mark for using a thermometer, 1 mark for reason it is safe.

short.q: Describe how heat is used in cooking and warming in a home.
short.answer: Heat from fire, gas or electricity cooks food making it soft and safer. Heat from fire or clothes keeps the body warm and chicks warm.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four points.

short.q: Explain why cooking pots are made of metal but their handles are not.
short.answer: Metal passes heat quickly to the food so it cooks. Handles made of wood or plastic pass heat slowly so our hands do not burn.
short.working: 2 marks for the pot and 2 marks for the handle.

short.q: Describe how to make a pair of kitchen gloves from local materials.
short.answer: Choose thick cotton cloth or old towel. Trace and cut two mitten shapes. Add an inner layer. Sew them together leaving the wrist open. Turn it inside out.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: Name four safety measures to observe in a kitchen and give a reason for each.
short.answer: Handles inwards to avoid knocking pots, gloves to avoid burns, children away to avoid accidents, switch off iron to avoid fire.
short.working: 1 mark for each with reason.

short.q: Explain the difference between heat and temperature.
short.answer: Heat is energy that makes things hot. Temperature is how hot something is and it is measured with a thermometer in degrees Celsius.
short.working: 2 marks for heat and 2 marks for temperature.

short.q: Give four ways in which heat is used in farming.
short.answer: Drying grain and crops, hatching chicks, keeping chicks warm, cooking, controlling pests, drying fish.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain the importance of heat in daily life.
short.answer: Heat keeps us warm, cooks food, dries clothes and crops, helps plants grow, makes rain by evaporation, and is used to make metals and glass.
short.working: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

short.q: Describe safety measures to be observed when handling heat at home and at school.
short.answer: Do not play with matches, keep children from fires, use gloves, turn handles inwards, switch off cookers and irons, keep fuels away from fire, cool burns with water and tell an adult.
short.working: 1 mark for each measure up to 5.

short.q: Describe an activity that shows the uses of heat, for example drying clothes in different conditions.
short.answer: Wet two similar cloths. Hang one in the sun and the other in the shade. After some time, feel them. The cloth in the sun dries faster because heat from the sun evaporates the water.
short.working: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for fair comparison, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.
